headline: KSE-100 jumped 1.2% Monday Aug 3 to close at 178,200.02 (+2,105.91 pts, intraday +1.64%) on US-Iran peace hopes after Trump held off a fresh strike on Iran — banks, cement, E&P, OMCs and power led. Drawdown from the Jan ATH narrows to ~6.0%, still well short of the 10% deploy-dry-powder line. Note: Mali's own price feed (data/prices.json) has NOT yet posted today's session — it still carries Friday Jul 31's close as of this review; live third-party quotes confirm the rally and put AVN at ~Rs 31.54 (-0.5%, lagging the market again). AVN's sell-half plan — due Mon Jul 27 and reiterated as "execute at Monday Aug 3's open" in the last two reviews — is, as of this review, STILL showing the full 24,500 shares in holdings; today was the stated execution day. This is the fifteenth straight review flagging it. EFERT's confirmed H1 2026 dividend record date (Rs 1.75/share) is Mon Aug 10 — 7 days out, not yet in the 3-day notification window.
market: PSX opened the new week with a strong rally: the KSE-100 gained as much as 2,891.83 points (+1.64%) intraday, hitting 178,985.94, before settling up 1.2% at 178,200.02 (+2,105.91 pts) — driven entirely by geopolitics rather than local fundamentals. President Trump held off an imminent attack on Iran to pursue a deal reopening the Strait of Hormuz, easing oil-price and shipping-disruption fears; Brent pulled back to roughly $94-98/bbl, a tailwind for oil-importing Pakistan. Buying was broad-based across index heavyweights — HBL, MCB, MEBL, NBP, OGDC, PPL, POL, PSO and HUBCO all traded green — spanning commercial banks, cement, E&P, OMCs and power generation. Against the Jan 23, 2026 all-time high of 189,556, the drawdown narrows to roughly 6.0%, moving further from (not closer to) the 10% line that would trigger deploying the AICF/MICF cash reserve — no change to the dry-powder plan. SBP's policy rate remains at 11.5% (held Jul 27); the IMF's EFF/RSF program stays on track (third/second reviews completed May 2026, ~$4.8B disbursed to date, reserves ~$16B and rebuilding) — stable macro backdrop, nothing new this week. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: Mali's own data/prices.json has not been updated for today's session as of this review (git pull still shows Friday Jul 31's close, last commit 2026-08-02 20:17 UTC) — the P/L figures below and in the app are one session stale; today's rally is not yet reflected in the portfolio value. Live web quotes (not yet in the app) confirm the broad-market move and show AVN trading around Rs 31.54, down ~0.5% even as the index rallied 1.2% — the stock keeps lagging on every up day, consistent with the deteriorating-fundamentals thesis rather than reversing it. On holdings: EFERT's H1 2026 results remain as confirmed Jul 30 from the PSX filing — consolidated H1 profit Rs 7.12B (-15.9% YoY), EPS Rs 5.33 (vs Rs 6.34), standalone entity worse (-34.6% YoY), cushioned by a one-off Rs 1.8B SIDC remeasurement gain; a genuine earnings decline confirming the glut thesis. The board still declared a Rs 1.75/share (17.5%) interim dividend, record date Monday Aug 10, 2026 (book closure Aug 11-12) — now 7 days out, still outside the 3-day notify window. AVN: holdings data (index.html DEFAULT_HOLDINGS) still shows the full 24,500-share position on the exact day the sell-half plan was due to execute ("Monday Aug 3's open" per the prior two reviews) — fifteen consecutive reviews have now flagged this without a corresponding update to holdings; either the trade hasn't been placed, or it has and the app just hasn't been told. AVN's next earnings report is confirmed for Sep 2, 2026 — the outside deadline for a full exit if there's still no recovery. CPHL: no update since the Jul 8 REIT-demerger board approval (two Lahore properties, 4.1 and 27.15 kanal, into Citi Core Holdings for 331.72M new shares) — still just a value-unlock story in motion, no urgency either way. Technical note: as of the last successful price-feed run (Aug 2, 20:17 UTC), the fund NAV side (ASSF, AKDISSF, NISIF, NISF, MIF, AICF, MICF, AKDISIF) was still moving day to day, so the earlier "frozen NAV" concern from late July appears resolved — but today's missing update is a new, separate feed gap worth a look at scripts/fetch_prices.py or the GitHub Action schedule.

Keep for yield given the dividend held up, but this is now the second straight half with declining core earnings — rotate out if Q3/Q4 offtake doesn't recover or the next dividend gets cut outright.
